overview: The WBCS (Exe.) etc. Examination is run by the Public Service Commission, West Bengal. It fills posts in four groups. Group A covers WBCS (Executive) and other Group A services. Group B is the West Bengal Police Service. Group C and Group D cover a range of state posts. You fill in one application and can choose one or more groups. There are three stages. The first is the Preliminary exam, a 200-mark objective (MCQ) screening test. The second is the Main exam, with six compulsory papers, and Group A and B candidates also take one optional subject of two papers. The third is the Personality Test. Prelims marks are used only for screening. Your final rank comes from the Main and the Personality Test marks added together. For the 2024 cycle, applications ran from 18 November 2025 to 17 December 2025. The Prelims took place on 14 June 2026, and WBPSC published the final answer key on 27 August 2026. As of 2 October 2026, WBPSC had not announced the Prelims result or the Main exam dates. The 2024 exam uses the older scheme from the 2014 notification. WBPSC has said that a new scheme (P&AR Notification No. 695-PAR dated 17 June 2025) will apply from the WBCS 2025 exam. The next cycle, WBCS 2025, has only an indicative advertisement so far (No. 03/2025, dated 29 November 2025).

It also says posts in a group may not be filled if the department does not report vacancies in time. As of 2 October 2026, no WBCS 2024 vacancy list was found on the WBPSC website. Some vacancies may be reserved for EWS, SC, ST, OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) and PwBD candidates of West Bengal. Reservation for Meritorious Sportspersons applies only to Group D posts.

pattern.mode: Offline objective (MCQ) test. You mark answers on an OMR sheet with a black ball-point pen.

sections.name: Current Events of National & International Importance

pattern.marking: There is one paper, General Studies, with 200 questions worth 200 marks. All questions carry equal marks, so each correct answer gets 1 mark. Each wrong answer loses 0.25 mark, as printed on the 2024 question booklet.
notes: Each of the 8 areas carries 25 marks. Because all questions carry equal marks, this works out to 25 questions per area.
Each question has four options, (A) to (D). Marking more than one circle counts as a wrong answer.
The Prelims is only a screening test. Its marks are not added to your final merit score.
Only candidates who qualify in the Prelims of a given year can sit the Main exam of that same year.
The paper is set at the level of a graduate in any subject.
The exam is held in Kolkata and in district centres across West Bengal. In 2024 there were 25 district centres.
In the 2024 final answer key, every candidate gets 1 mark for each question marked '*', whether or not they attempted it.

pattern.mode: Offline written exam. Four compulsory papers are MCQ, answered on OMR sheets. Papers I and II (languages) and the optional papers are conventional (descriptive) answer papers.

sections.name: Paper I – Bengali/Hindi/Urdu/Nepali/Santali (letter or report writing, précis, composition, translation from English) – conventional
Paper II – English (letter or report writing, précis, composition, translation into English) – conventional
Paper III – General Studies-I (Indian History with emphasis on National Movement; Geography of India with reference to West Bengal) – MCQ
Paper IV – General Studies-II (Science & Technology, Environment, General Knowledge, Current Affairs) – MCQ
Paper V – The Constitution of India and Indian Economy including role and functions of RBI – MCQ
Paper VI – Arithmetic and Test of Reasoning – MCQ
Optional Subject Paper 1 (Group A and B candidates only) – conventional
Optional Subject Paper 2 (Group A and B candidates only) – conventional

pattern.marking: Each paper carries 200 marks. Every wrong answer in an MCQ paper carries negative marking, at the rate printed on the question booklet. If you reveal your identity in an answer script (for example your name or roll number), 10% of that paper's full marks will be cut.
notes: Group A and B candidates write all 6 compulsory papers plus one optional subject of two papers, for 1600 marks.
Group C and D candidates write only the 6 compulsory papers, for 1200 marks.
For Paper I you pick one language: Bengali, Hindi, Urdu, Nepali or Santali. Paper II asks you to translate from that language into English.

You can answer every paper except the language papers in English or Bengali, but you must use only one language within a paper. The Political Science and Botany optionals may also be answered in Nepali.
The scheme says Santali papers are set in the Ol Chiki script and must be answered in Ol Chiki.
There are 38 optional subjects to choose from. The optional papers are at about Honours degree level. Law, Medical Science and Engineering are at LLB, MBBS and BE level.
WBPSC can set qualifying marks in any paper and in the aggregate. If you fail to reach the qualifying mark in a paper, that paper is left out of your aggregate.
The official scheme does not say how many questions each MCQ paper has.

pattern.mode: Interview at the Public Service Commission office, Kolkata
pattern.duration: Not stated in the official scheme
pattern.marking: Each candidate has one Personality Test. Marks are then given separately for each group applied for, out of 200 (A & B), 150 (C) or 100 (D).
notes: Candidates are called in order of merit based on their Main exam results.
Your final merit is based on your Main exam marks plus your Personality Test marks.
Maximum total marks are 1800 for Group A, 1800 for Group B, 1350 for Group C and 1300 for Group D.
Group B (West Bengal Police Service) candidates are specially tested for suitability for police service.
If your mother tongue is not Bengali or Nepali, your knowledge of Bengali is tested at the Personality Test.

To qualify, your aggregate (written plus Personality Test) must reach at least: UR 40%, EWS 40%, OBC (A & B) 38%, SC 35%, ST 30%, PwBD 30%, MSP 40%. WBPSC may relax these marks for reserved categories.
If two candidates tie, the higher Personality Test mark ranks first. Next comes the higher compulsory aggregate, then the best compulsory papers, and finally the older candidate.

eligibility.nationality: You must be a citizen of India, by birth or by registration, or a national of another country that the Government of India has declared eligible. Candidates in the second category need an eligibility certificate from the Government before they can be offered an appointment.

age.summary: Age is counted on 1 January 2024. Group A and C: 21 to 36 years (born between 2 January 1988 and 1 January 2003). Group B (West Bengal Police Service): 20 to 36 years (born between 2 January 1988 and 1 January 2004). Group D: 21 to 39 years (born between 2 January 1985 and 1 January 2003). If you are between 20 and 21 (born between 1 January 2003 and 1 January 2004), you can apply for Group B only. WBPSC accepts only the age recorded in your Madhyamik or equivalent certificate.

education.posts: All groups (A, B, C and D)
education.requirement: A degree from a recognised university. You must hold it by the closing date of the application.

education.posts: West Bengal Junior Social Welfare Service (Group C) – posts in Homes for the Blind and/or Deaf
education.requirement: A degree, diploma or certificate in training the blind and/or deaf is essential. Candidates without it can still be appointed, but must complete in-service training.

other: Language: You must be able to read, write and speak Bengali. This does not apply if your mother tongue is Nepali. If your mother tongue is neither Bengali nor Nepali, your Bengali will be tested at the Personality Test, and poor performance can lead to cancellation of your candidature.

West Bengal Subordinate Land Revenue Service, Grade-I needs a good working knowledge of written and spoken Bengali. Candidates whose mother tongue is Nepali are exempt, but must pass a departmental Bengali exam within two years. Selected candidates also go through 6 months of in-service training.

Physical standard for Group B (West Bengal Police Service): minimum height 1.65 m for men and 1.50 m for women. The height rule is relaxed for groups such as Gorkhas, Garhwalis and Assamese tribals. You must state your height in the application form.
You must have good health and good character. Selected candidates must pass a medical board and a police verification of antecedents.

Reservation benefits for EWS, SC, ST and OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) apply only to candidates of West Bengal. You need a certificate from a West Bengal competent authority, issued on or before the closing date.
Reservation for Meritorious Sportspersons applies only to Group D posts.
Submit only one application and choose your group(s) in it. You cannot change your groups later. More than one application from the same person may be cancelled.
Fee: ₹210 plus service charges, paid online. SC/ST candidates of West Bengal and PwBD candidates (40% and above) do not pay a fee. OBC candidates pay the full fee.

faqs.q: Which WBCS exam is the latest, and where does it stand now?
faqs.a: The latest is the WBCS (Exe.) etc. Examination 2024 (Advt. No. 08/2024). The Prelims took place on 14 June 2026, and the final answer key came out on 27 August 2026. As of 2 October 2026, the Prelims result and the Main exam dates had not been announced. For WBCS 2025, there is only an indicative advertisement (No. 03/2025). WBPSC says a new scheme will apply from the 2025 exam.

faqs.q: What is the WBCS Prelims pattern and negative marking?
faqs.a: There is one General Studies paper with 200 MCQs worth 200 marks, and you get 2½ hours. The paper covers 8 areas of 25 marks each. A correct answer gets 1 mark. The 2024 question booklet says 0.25 mark is cut for each wrong answer.

faqs.q: Do Prelims marks count in the final merit list?
faqs.a: No. The Prelims only decides who goes on to the Main exam. Your final merit is based on your Main exam marks plus your Personality Test marks.

faqs.q: What is the age limit for WBCS 2024?
faqs.a: Age is counted on 1 January 2024. Groups A and C: 21–36 years. Group B (Police): 20–36 years. Group D: 21–39 years. SC/ST candidates of West Bengal get 5 extra years, OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) candidates of West Bengal get 3, and PwBD candidates can apply up to age 45.

faqs.q: Do I need to know Bengali to apply?
faqs.a: Yes. You must be able to read, write and speak Bengali, unless your mother tongue is Nepali. If your mother tongue is neither Bengali nor Nepali, your Bengali will be tested at the Personality Test, and a poor result can cancel your candidature.

faqs.q: Which Main exam papers do I write for each group?
faqs.a: Every candidate writes six compulsory papers of 200 marks each. Papers I and II are descriptive language papers, and Papers III to VI are MCQ. Group A and B candidates also take one optional subject of two 200-mark papers. Maximum totals, including the Personality Test, are 1800 for Groups A and B, 1350 for Group C and 1300 for Group D.

calculator.note: WBCS Prelims 2024 has 200 questions of equal value for 200 marks, so each correct answer gets 1 mark. The 2024 question booklet says 0.25 mark is cut for each wrong answer. Each of the 8 areas carries 25 marks, which means 25 questions per area. Prelims marks are used only to pick candidates for the Main exam. They do not count in the final merit.
